newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- better tone, but quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- better tone, but quiet.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were showing strength at midday Friday, but traders said it was hard to find the kind of gains Treasuries scored on the strength of a tame Producer Price Index.

The government market was up 19/32 at 101-12/32. That pushed the yield down to 6.52 percent, after the Labor Department reported earlier in the day that June producer prices fell 0.1 percent overall and rose 0.1 percent when food and energy prices were excluded.
Analysts, who were expecting an unchanged overall rate, said the figure meant that the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates again soon.
Despite the large uptick in Treasuries, municipal secondary prices were mostly flat.
In follow-through action from Thursday's new issues, Goldman Sachs & Co. said it closed the account on a $40 million Kansas City, Mo., general obligation competitive deal.
In the muni secondary market, Allegheny County Sanitary Authority Pa., MBIA 5-3/8s of 2024 were bid at 5.51 percent, down one basis point from the close on Thursday.
And Dade County, Fla., FGIC 5-1/4s of 2021 were bid at 5.45 percent, unchanged.
In futures, the September municipal contract rose 11/32 to 119-22/32, while September T-bonds gained 15/32 to 114-11/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 171 from 175 at the close on Thursday.
